decisions.scan_shows: A V-shaped bowl is followed by one separate upright. There is a transverse stroke above and a heavier transverse rule below. Main confirms VI and both rules with all readers; H gives the same Roman value without either rule.

A small a is followed by two long descending p constructions, low joined e/n strokes, a tall looped d, a separate dot above i and an open c leading to the final e sweep. Main agrees with all three readers that appendice is readable; C’s doubt is removed.

Before the independently beginning tall l of lettre is a separate large l loop with a low rightward a exit and terminal turn. Main confirms la lettre with all three readers and H; witness C omits the separate la.
Two separate crossed X forms and one upright are visible between the upper and lower transverse lines. Main confirms ruled XXI. H has the same value but omits the two rules.

The second word again has a small a, two deep p descenders, joined e/n strokes, the looped d, a separate i dot and the low c/e ending before the colon. Main resolves appendice with all readers from this occurrence’s own strokes.

decisions.place: Third entry, relation/relations after the colon
decisions.scan_shows: The r/e beginning, tall l, low a, crossed t and dotted i are followed by a compressed low ending. Its long rightward stroke and short terminal down-turn can be the n exit or include a closely merged s; there is no secure additional boundary. Main agrees with all readers on relation/relations, preferring singular. Witness C is certain singular and H certain plural, so the uncertainty differs from both.

A tall crossed t leads into a small o, joined r/s turns, a separately dotted i and low o/n ending. The final n has a long rightward exit and short terminal hook. Main confirms torsion and removes C’s doubt.

The open c and small o lead to a tall looped h; the low o/m/o members are joined but distinguishable, followed by a tall l, a further o and long descending g loop. The dotted i and terminal e remain separate. Main confirms cohomologie with all readers.

decisions.place: Slanted left marginal note, ruled XXIII
decisions.scan_shows: The rotated margin crop shows two crossed X forms followed by three distinct upright strokes, with a transverse line above and another below. The surrounding words read faire un / exposé, with a separate acute, and a question mark follows the numeral. Main confirms the complete margin reading; the substantive H difference is omission of the two numeral rules.

Two crossed X forms are followed by two separate upright strokes, the first shorter than the second. The upper transverse line and shorter lower rule are both visible. Main confirms ruled XXII with all readers; H omits the rules.

After the dotted i and small r turn, the final low sweep rises slightly and ends in a down-hook. C-reader takes that hook as a distinct s. Main agrees with A/B that the merged stroke does not securely separate an added s from the preceding e’s exit, so Commentaires/Commentaire is retained, plural first. H gives the plural without a doubt mark.

The initial c/r and dotted i are followed by a clear s, crossed t, a, two tall l loops, a second dotted i and the n/e sweep. A detached low full stop follows. Main agrees with all readers that cristalline is readable and removes C’s doubt without changing the period.

notes:
Undated handwritten planning list on printed ‘INSTITUT / DES HAUTES ÉTUDES SCIENTIFIQUES’ stationery. ‘SGA 7’ is enclosed by a pale loop; there is no other title, signature, own page number or total count. Archive 76 is a comment. Four main entries form two brace groups. The upper pair concerns numerical references and ‘appendice : la lettre Deligne 2 pages’; ‘2 pages’ is the writer’s stated count for that letter. The lower pair concerns torsion and crystalline cohomology, followed by a slanted marginal proposal for another exposé.

The writer’s own questions are the mark after ‘1.15 - 1.22’, ‘Refaire 1.14 ?’, the parenthesized ‘(?)’ beside XXII, and ‘faire un exposé XXIII ?’ in the margin. They are preserved separately from editorial uncertainty. No mathematical proof or calculation is presented or checked. The heavily retraced first numeral and brace do not expose an independently readable cancelled predecessor. All ten C doubt occurrences are recorded: six resolve, four remain, and relation/relations is a new uncertainty. The main text adds C’s omitted ‘la’ and the visible extra lower brace contour. H’s descriptions of the printed block and graphics, its omitted numeral rules and its different certainty are collated without turning its editorial notes into manuscript text.
math_reading_decisions: Each Roman group was read independently. The first remains VI/VII because central traces merge beside the brace; the later groups read VI, XXI, XXII and marginal XXIII. All have upper and lower transverse strokes. The clear following VI does not decide the first group.

The decimal references retain low points and the sequence 1.11, 1.14, 1.15, 1.22, then Refaire 1.14. The last digit is resolved to 2 from its hooked descent and lower-left return; no numerical expectation is used. The separator between the ranges is a short unheaded dash, not an arrow.

The separator between 1.11 and 1.14 remains colon/à, colon preferred from its two detached members and absent right-hand a tail. This does not establish how the writer intended the references to be rearranged.

The free and parenthesized question marks and the periods after coh. and final cristalline are preserved. The high straight line above the first references belongs to the printed letterhead, not to a mathematical expression.
The marginal exposé has a visible acute and XXIII has three individual terminal uprights. These are reading checks only. The reference and brace comparisons are not mathematical proof events.
